source: NCERT Class XI, Performing Arts & Cultural Heritage of India, Ch. 7 (UNESCO Heritage: World Heritage Sites and Intangible Cultural Heritage).

sections.heading: 1. UNESCO and the World Heritage Concept
points: **UNESCO** (UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation) adopted the **World Heritage Convention (1972)** to protect sites of **'outstanding universal value'**.
World Heritage Sites are of three kinds: **cultural, natural, and mixed**.
India has **40+ World Heritage Sites** (one of the highest numbers).

sections.heading: 2. India's Cultural World Heritage Sites (Examples)
points: **Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb** (Mughal/Sultanate).
**Ajanta and Ellora caves, Elephanta caves, Sanchi Stupa, Mahabalipuram, Khajuraho, Konark Sun Temple, Hampi, Pattadakal, Great Chola Temples**.
**Jaipur city, Ahmedabad (first Indian World Heritage City), Champaner, Rani-ki-Vav (Patan), Nalanda, Dholavira, Santiniketan, Hoysala temples**.
**Mountain Railways of India, Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (Mumbai)**.

sections.heading: 3. India's Natural and Mixed Sites
points: **Natural:** **Kaziranga, Keoladeo, Manas, Sundarbans, Nanda Devi & Valley of Flowers, Western Ghats, Great Himalayan National Park**.
**Mixed:** **Khangchendzonga National Park (Sikkim)** — India's only mixed (cultural + natural) site.

sections.heading: 4. Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH)
points: **ICH** = living traditions — oral traditions, performing arts, rituals, festive events, crafts (protected under the **2003 Convention**).

India's ICH on the UNESCO list: **Kutiyattam, Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Ramman, Mudiyettu, Kalbelia, Chhau, Buddhist chanting of Ladakh, Manipuri Sankirtana, Thatheras of Jandiala Guru (brass/copper craft), Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja of Kolkata, Garba of Gujarat**.
The **Kumbh Mela** is the largest peaceful congregation; **Yoga** and **Durga Puja** are widely known.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: World Heritage Convention = 1972; ICH Convention = 2003.
Sites are cultural, natural or mixed; Khangchendzonga = India's only mixed site.
Ahmedabad = India's first UNESCO World Heritage City.
ICH examples: Kutiyattam, Ramlila, Kalbelia, Chhau, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja, Garba.
India has 40+ World Heritage Sites.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **World Heritage Convention = 1972**; **Intangible Cultural Heritage Convention = 2003**.
**Khangchendzonga (Sikkim)** is India's **only mixed** World Heritage Site.
**Ahmedabad** was India's **first World Heritage City**.
**Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja (Kolkata), Garba** are on the **Intangible** heritage list.
